sentences.text:
This Criminal Appeal has been filed challenging the Judgment dated 12.01.2023 passed in S.C.No.373 of 2021 by the Sessions Judge, Mahalir Neethimandram, Allikulam, Chennai, thereby convicted the appellant for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(1) read with 511 of IPC.
2.

entities.text: Sessions Judge, Mahalir Neethimandram, Allikulam, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant is the accused herein.

The case of the prosecution is that on 05.07.2021 at about 2.30 p.m., P.W.2, who was engaged in supplying water cans at Md.Abdullah 2nd Street, Chepauk,
heard screams of a woman from a nearby dilapidated building.
When he went near the building and looked through a screen, he found a woman lying half-naked with a man over her.
The woman had no clothes on her lower body.
P.W.2 immediately raised an alarm, upon which the nearby residents rushed to the spot.
On seeing the crowd, the appellant came out of the building and fled from the scene.
P.W.2 identified the appellant when he returned to the place of occurrence and began quarrelling with others.

At that time, P.W.1, who had come to collect his friend's motorcycle, which was parked near the spot, found the appellant https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
25/10/2025 04:04:43 pm ) quarrellying with some persons and he also heard the cries of a woman coming from inside of the dilapidated building.
On entering the building, he found the victim in a half-naked condition.
He immediately instructed the transgenders, who were present in the scene of occurrence, to assist in rescuing the woman from the building.

3. Thereafter, P.W.1 informed the police through his friend, based on which, a complaint was lodged and an FIR in Crime No.3 of 2021 was registered for the offences under Sections 354A, 354D, 376 of IPC and Section 4 of Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: After completion of investigation, a final report was filed for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(1) of IPC.
4. On the side of the prosecution, P.Ws.1 to 11 were examined and Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.
On the side of the appellant, no witnesses were examined and no documents were marked.

On a perusal of the oral and documentary evidence, the Trial Court found the appellant guilty of the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(1) read with 511 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 25/10/2025 04:04:43 pm ) a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months.
Aggrieved by the same, the present Criminal Appeal has been filed.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that there was no witnesses to the occurrence.
There are contradictions between the prosecution witnesses.
The victim was straight away brought to the home and was not subjected to medical examination immediately after the incident.
The person, who identified the appellant, was not examined by the prosecution.

Though the victim was subjected to medical examination, the medical evidence does not support the case of the prosecution, since the Doctor did not find any injuries on the victim's body, indicating that there was no possibility of sexual assault.
Further, the two transgenders who were present at the time of occurrence were also not examined by the prosecution.

Therefore, even then, the Trial Court,
without properly appreciating the evidence on record, has mechanically convicted the appellant and as such, the conviction and sentence cannot be sustained and are liable to be set aside.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned Additional Pubic Prosecutor appearing for the respondent submitted that P.W.1 is the volunteer who was engaged in social services during the COVID-19 period.
He is not related to the appellant in any way and had absolutely no motive to lodge a false complaint against the appellant.
He did not know the appellant prior to the occurrence.
P.Ws.1 and 2 rescued the victim and lodged the complaint.
In fact, P.W.2 had witnessed the appellant committing to rape on the victim.
The victim, being mentally retarded, was not examined as a witness before the Trial Court.
However, the persons who rescued the victim from the hands of the appellant were examined as prosecution witnesses and their evidence clearly proved the charges against the appellant.

Hence,
the Trial Court rightly appreciated the evidence and convicted the appellant and therefore, the Judgment of conviction and sentence does not warrant any interference of this Court.
7.
Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
8. Admittedly, the victim is a mentally retarded person and was not in a position to depose before the Trial Court.
P.Ws.1 and 2 were the persons who rescued the victim from the hands of the appellant.
P.W.1 is working as a teacher and used to voluntarily engage in social service activities during COVID-19 pandamic, particularly in rescue activities.
P.W.2 is working as a coolie, engaged in the business of delivering water cans.
P.W.3 is working as Event Manager and is also running NGO under the name and style of Anbin Paadai, which engages in various social service activities.
Therefore, it is evident that P.Ws.1 to 3 are independent witnesses having no motive to falsely implicate the appellant.
9. While being so, on 05.07.2021, P.Ws.1 & 2 had witnessed the appellant attempting to commit rape on the victim.
They immediately intervened and rescued the victim and lodged a police complaint.
Thereafter, the victim was subjected to medical examination for sexual offence.
The prosecution also produced relevant medical evidence to prove the mental condition of the victim.

P.W.1 deposed that, on the date of occurrence, when he went to the place of occurrence https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 25/10/2025 04:04:43 pm ) to collect his friend's motorcycle, he heard the cries of a woman from a nearby dilapidated building.
On entering, he found the victim lying half- naked.
He immediately sought for help from a few transgenders who were present in the scene of occurrence and provided clothes to the victim and rescued her.
Immediately, he called the police and also informed to the home.
He also stated that immediately after the occurrence, he saw the appellant quarrelling with some persons in front of a wine shop and thereafter, he fled from the scene.
Later, he was identified by other witnesses.
10. The evidence of P.W.1 is categorically corroborated by P.W.2, who is also an eye witness to the occurrence.

P.W.2 deposed that he heard the screams of a woman and upon reaching the spot,
found the victim lying half naked, while the appellant was committing rape on her.

Therefore,
P.W.3, who came from the home, was examined and he identified the victim and confirmed that she had been subjected to sexual assault by the appellant.
Therefore, the P.Ws.1 to 3 identified the appellant and categorically deposed that he was committing rape on the victim.

sentences.text: Though there are minor discrepancies in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, the same would not be fatal to the case of the prosecution.
During medical examination, P.W.8 found that the victim was mentally ill and had external injuries on her body.
However, her hymen was not intact and that there was swelling in her abdominal and thigh regions.
With regard to her mental condition, P.W.9 examined her and deposed that the victim is mentally disordered and had the mental growth of a child aged about eight years.
Therefore, the prosecution proved the charges beyond reasonable doubts that the appellant had committed offence punishable under Section 376(2)(1) read with 511 of IPC.
Therefore, the Trial Court rightly convicted the appellant.

12. In view of the above discussions, this Court finds no infirmity or illegality in the Judgment dated 12.01.2023 passed in S.C.No.373 of 2021 by the Sessions Judge, Mahalir Neethimandram,
Allikulam, Chennai.
Accordingly, this Criminal Appeal stands dismissed.
However, the respondent is directed to secure the petitioner to undergo the remaining period of sentence forthwith.

13. In the result, this Criminal Appeal stands dismissed.
